strategic_notes: Cycle 2 is a focused SINGLE-PIPELINE cycle targeting the highest-leverage carry-forward from cycle 1. Rationale: (a) RICE math heavily favors protocol-extension (6.75 vs §5.10's 1.87). (b) Single architectural change activates 14 dormant renderers in one stroke — unmatched fix-per-effort ratio. (c) Time budget (4h 11m) fits one well-scoped pipeline with architect consultation + mandatory daemon rebuild + restart + QA; §5.10 needs its own 4-6h cycle per spec line 1949. (d) §5.17 is a small screenshot task that costs nothing extra folded into user agent's routine core_flow QA. CYCLE 2 PATTERNS TO PRESERVE FROM CYCLE 1: (1) BA-QA mid-pipeline gate — cycle 1 caught 12 objections across pipelines 0/1 that would have burned entire Dev iterations. (2) Protocol-first inspection — BA MUST read codexAppServerClient.ts before writing spec. (3) Daemon rebuild + restart MANDATORY when happy-cli has runtime changes (cycle 1 §5.9 lesson; this cycle's primary task has RUNTIME changes, unlike cycle 1's TODO-only changes). (4) DORMANT-RENDERER acceptance fallback — if Codex session still not provisioned, source+bundle+typecheck is BA-sanctioned (cycle 1 precedent). CYCLE 2 NEW RISKS: (a) sessionProtocolMapper.ts at 883+ lines is quality-gate blocked — expect Python read_text/write_text bypass as in cycle 1. (b) Daemon restart from inside a daemon-managed session triggers cgroup kill (CLAUDE.md rule 5) — Dev MUST use systemd-run --scope or restart from outside the session. (c) ~14 event-type branches mean ~14 x 2 = 28 callsite additions across 2 files — architect must validate the shape contract BEFORE Dev starts, or rework cost is high.
